transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - Catalyst), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Dana Ortiz (Head of Product)

Summary (auto): Integration discovery for Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private, focus on SDK integrations, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy architecture, quotas and observability hooks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, I'll hand it off to Ethan to cover the integration details, quick intro then we can dig into your requirements.
[00:12] Ethan: Hi Priya, Marcus, Dana. Quick one liner - Redwood provides hosted API but also Dedicated reserved pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. Today we'll focus on how you'd integrate - SDKs, LangChain, gateway, quotas and observability.
[00:30] Priya: Great, thanks. We are trying to understand where Redwood would sit in our stack. Right now we call a couple of models via a gateway to keep credentials in one place, most calls go through our edge proxy but we also have server-side batch jobs.
[00:47] Marcus: yeah and our main concerns are latency for real-time checkout suggestions, cost per token for high-volume previews, and obviously PCI and data residency - though we redact card data before hitting any model.
[01:05] Ethan: Makes sense. On the integration side we have first-class SDKs in JS/Python, plus example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. For gateway setups you can either route through your proxy to our REST endpoints or use short-lived API keys and let each service call Redwood directly. Both patterns are supported.
[01:25] Dana: do you have a recommended pattern for a microservices architecture? we run product search as a separate service and checkout suggestion as another.
[01:35] Ethan: If you want centralized credential management and single throttling point, proxying through your gateway is common; you lose a bit of client-side observability unless you propagate trace ids. Another approach is to mint ephemeral keys from your auth layer and call Redwood directly; that gives per-service metrics and easier per-route quotas.
[01:55] Marcus: ephemerals sound interesting, but we need SSO and RBAC - can Redwood integrate with our SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[02:06] Sofia: yes, for Dedicated and Private customers we support SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC controls in the console. Hosted customers get SSO for enterprise plans.
[02:18] Priya: security is huge for us. we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and a SOC2 report. Also we may need VPC peering for a private control plane.
[02:30] Ethan: we can provide SOC2, and we support KMS for key wrapping in Dedicated/Private. VPC peering and private control plane are available on the Private product; Dedicated can be configured with strict network controls as well. We'll include diagrams.
[02:45] Marcus: great. On the SDK side - is there an official LangChain adapter? we've built a lot on top of LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[02:52] Ethan: Yes, we have sample LangChain chains and a LlamaIndex connector in our repo. They show streaming responses and function calling patterns. The samples include an example for streaming token-by-token to a websocket and for capturing the token-level cost.
[03:10] Dana: token-level cost, how is that surfaced? we need per-route cost breakdowns for finance.
[03:18] Ethan: Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route and per-model. For Dedicated you can export usage logs or ship metrics to Datadog/OpenTelemetry; we also expose a usage events API for custom billing.
[03:32] Priya: and about quotas - can we enforce per-tenant quotas inside Redwood? we have multi-tenant customers and need per-tenant throttling.
[03:40] Sofia: yes, you can create routes and per-route quotas; for Dedicated you can also set workspace-level limits. For advanced isolation we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity and burst policies.
[03:55] Marcus: how about graceful degradation? if Dedicated capacity is saturated do you offer fallback to smaller hosted variants?
[04:03] Ethan: Smart routing supports fallbacks - you can set policies to route to a lower-cost model or region if capacity is constrained. For strict SLOs you'd pin a model on Dedicated.
[04:15] Marcus: what's the typical latency on Dedicated for those small sequence lengths we use (like 64 tokens)?
[04:23] Ethan: On modern GPU pools we often see 20-60ms per token reactive latency; for short 64 token responses 95th can be under 200ms with proper batching disabled for low-latency routes. We'll share our perf profiles.
[04:36] Priya: curious about batching - we do a mix of high QPS for previews and occasional low-latency checkout calls. we don't want batching to add unpredictable latency to checkout.
[04:48] Ethan: Redwood supports route-level batching policies; you can disable batching for critical routes and enable aggressive batching for background preview pipelines which reduces cost. Also prefix/KV caching can dramatically cut cost for repeated prompts.
[05:02] Dana: can we run the inference inside our VPC? for some regulated customers we need on-prem or air-gapped options.
[05:10] Sofia: Private (VPC/on-prem) supports that; the control plane can be on Redwood or customer-managed and we provide an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments. Most customers start with Dedicated, then for regulated workloads move to Private.
[05:25] Marcus: log forwarding - we use Splunk and Datadog. can you ship traces and logs?
[05:31] Ethan: yes, we expose OpenTelemetry traces and metrics, plus native Datadog integration. You can stream audit logs and request/response metadata to your SIEM (with PII redaction controls).
[05:45] Priya: what's the SDK auth flow look like? we want short lived keys and granular scopes.
[05:51] Ethan: SDK supports OAuth-style token minting via your auth layer for ephemeral keys, and the SDKs accept those tokens; scopes can be limited to routes and models. We'll include an example of minting tokens from a gateway.
[06:03] Dana: any gotchas with LangChain - we've seen memory blowups with streaming and tool-calling.
[06:10] Ethan: common issues - streaming + tool-calling requires careful handling of partial deltas; our LangChain examples show recommended patterns and backpressure. Also set sensible max tokens for the chain and enable KV cache to reduce context growth.
[06:28] Marcus: okay let's talk POC. we want a Dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost under our traffic. ideally 2 weeks of benchmark with production-like traffic.
[06:37] Sofia: that sounds reasonable. For Dedicated pilot we can provision a small GPU pool and config autoscaling/burst to mimic your peak. We'll capture token-level cost and latency and hand over logs.
[06:48] Priya: what do we need to provide to get started?
[06:51] Ethan: sample traffic (preferably 48 hours), security requirements, redaction rules, and success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate). We'll run bench tests and share a results workbook.
[07:05] Marcus: timeline - we hope to decide in 2-3 weeks. Developer time available to help onboard.
[07:11] Sofia: we'll send a detailed next steps email with the security pack, LangChain samples, and a POC plan.
[07:18] Dana: about pricing - ballpark numbers for Dedicated?
[07:22] Sofia: depends on commit and GPU config; we'll send a tailored quote but expect reserved monthly pricing with overage at usage rates and potential discounts for annual commit.
[07:32] Priya: any references or customers in payments/commerce you can point to?
[07:35] Sofia: yes, we have a couple commerce customers; we'll include references and a benchmark deck.
[07:42] Marcus: ok thanks. a few clarifying questions - can we sandbox the observability export so it doesn't leak customer PII during the POC?
[07:51] Ethan: yes, we can configure redaction and sample only metadata, and we can provide masked payloads for the POC exports.
[07:59] Priya: and does Redwood support model pinning per route? we want deterministic outputs for the checkout flow.
[08:06] Ethan: yes, you can pin a model version to a route and pin to hardware type on Dedicated.
[08:15] Dana: for our engineers, could you share a short demo of the SDK and LangChain notebook?
[08:19] Sofia: we'll share a repo link and a short recorded demo.
[08:24] [Silence / background typing]
[08:40] Marcus: one more - rate limits, we need to throttle by tenant and also have burst allowance for occasional spikes.
[08:47] Ethan: per-route and per-tenant quotas + burst policies are supported in Dedicated; you can set reserve units and burst windows. We'll include sample config.
[08:58] Priya: ok great, thanks everyone.

[09:05] Sofia: recap - Redwood will: 1) send SOC2 and security pack + network diagrams, 2) share LangChain/LlamaIndex samples and SDK quickstart, 3) propose Dedicated pilot plan and pricing, 4) schedule POC benchmark next week if you confirm sample data.
[09:25] Marcus: sounds good. we'll get the 48h sample and our redaction rules over.
[09:32] Dana: thanks all, looking forward.

End of transcript.
